# Sodium — neutral atomic definition

The [existing Sodium master](../../records/0011-Sodium-Na/data/structured/0011-Sodium-Na.yaml) remains canonical and unchanged. The new [neutral atomic definition](../../records/0011-Sodium-Na/data/structured/0011-Sodium-Na-Neutral-Atom.yaml) identifies MAT:0011:ATOM:Na using the same reusable definition format as Neon. Its electron count follows the existing atomic number and the definition of neutral charge. Evidence is **DEFINITIONAL**, not an experimental measurement. No isotope, excitation, medium, temperature, pressure or thermochemical function is supplied.

All 89 existing Sodium files, including Na+ data, remain unchanged. No numerical source was accessed, allocated or admitted in this slice. The existing production thermochemistry adapter still refuses the current parent identity shape. A private crosswalk demonstrates a possible compatible representation and exercises the unchanged adapter guards; it is **DESIGNED**, not a canonical migration. Charged, wrong-electron, wrong-identity, molecular and measured-evidence substitutions are refused.

The first focused run passed eight checks. Recorded regression, integrity, publication and copy gates remain pending at the time of this note; inspect the actual terminal receipts. Prior Neon software evidence remains frozen at `.mat-local/thermal-neon-2026-10-08/final-cycle-proof.json`.

## Historical continuation — additive definition stage

Finish the Sodium neutral-owner validation/publication cycle at .mat-local/sodium-neutral-owner-2026-10-10/progress.json before another writer starts. Then review a reusable top-level-parent identity binding for the existing thermochemistry adapter, preserving the actual master bytes and Na+ data. The newly defined MAT:0011:ATOM:Na remains DEFINITIONAL; the current adapter still refuses the actual legacy parent shape. The private crosswalk is tested design, not an admitted binding or migration. Recheck physical/manifest union slots 011/013, independently review the retained Na GAS coefficients and 50 publisher rows including the 1170.525 K boundary, and resolve rights/source identity before any numerical accession. Do not invoke the unsafe legacy intake-review producer before its preservation repair.

Tracking: [existing selector](../../data/research/mat-update-review.json), [receipt](../../data/quality/sodium-neutral-owner-2026-10-10.json), [persistent handoff](../../MAT_CODEX_CONTINUATION_HANDOFF.md). MAT remains PARTIAL. Rights, independent source review, full domain acceptance and the 22 Sodium panels are not completed by an identity definition.

## Current checkpoint — explicit parent binding

The additive definition cycle subsequently passed validation, publication and byte-preservation checks for all 89 original Sodium files. The reusable [adapter](../../scripts/thermochemistry-context.mjs) and [schema](../../data/schema/1.0.0/thermochemistry-evaluation.schema.json) now support an explicit empty JSON Pointer for the unchanged master root. `/identity` retains its existing nested contract; `/` is not a root pointer. Both owner hashes, canonical identity, neutral counts, species, evidence and GAS context remain mandatory. There is no implicit shape fallback or Sodium-specific exception. No scientific record migration was required.

The [new regression tests](../../scripts/tests/thermochemistry-root-parent.test.mjs) use real unchanged Sodium owner bytes and rehashed invalid mutations. The targeted suite passed 53/53. An initial 13/14 run had one case-sensitive error-message expectation failure; its test snapshot and diagnostic remain preserved. Integration and output-copy checks are pending for this extension. No fit coefficients, measured values, source IDs or panel credit were added.

Finish the root-parent binding integration cycle at .mat-local/sodium-parent-binding-2026-10-10/progress.json and inspect actual terminal receipts before another writer starts. Then independently review Sodium NIST GAS coefficients and the 50 publisher rows, including the 1170.525 K boundary; recheck physical/manifest union slots 011/013 and resolve rights and source identity before numerical accession. No Sodium thermochemistry values or panels are admitted by the identity binding. Do not invoke the unsafe legacy intake-review producer before its preservation repair.

## Verified software cycle and final projection

The root-parent extension subsequently passed audit refresh, publication, full validation and byte-preservation/output-copy checks. All 89 original Sodium files and the definition remain unchanged; the copied schema also matches. The actual sealed proof is `.mat-local/sodium-parent-binding-2026-10-10/final-cycle-proof.json`. Final checkpoint projection remains pending at this timestamp; inspect the closure progress and receipts. Scientific acceptance stays PARTIAL.

Inspect .mat-local/sodium-parent-binding-2026-10-10/closure-progress.json and the closure terminal receipts before another writer starts. The explicit root-parent contract already passed 53 targeted tests, full validation, publication and original-owner preservation. Finish the final checkpoint projection if pending. Then review Sodium NIST GAS coefficients and the 50 publisher rows, including 1170.525 K; independently resolve source/rights and recheck physical/manifest slot union 011/013 before accession. No numerical Sodium values or standalone panels have been admitted. Do not invoke the unsafe legacy intake-review producer before its preservation repair.

## Numerical source review — candidate only

The final root-parent checkpoint projection closed with actual audit, publication, full validation, copy and owner-preservation passes at 2026-10-10T03:02:23.782Z. A new bounded private review uses the complete, hashed 8 October primary [WebBook Sodium GAS page](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440235&Units=SI&Mask=1) and its [publisher calculation table](https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7440235&Units=SI&Mask=1&Type=JANAFG&Table=on). Current web-tool retrieval attempts returned internal errors, so no fresh retrieval is claimed.

All 50 publisher rows and 150 heat-capacity, entropy and enthalpy-increment checks pass printed-value rounding tolerances in the existing Python and JavaScript implementations. The raw 1171 boundary label is retained, with an explicit calculation temperature of 1170.525 K supported by the source-fit endpoint inside the printed rounding cell. No extrapolation, room-temperature solid/liquid substitution or experimental-replication claim is made. The fourth table column remains verbatim and is not treated as one of the three checked quantities.

The separate [JANAF Sodium reference-state table](https://janaf.nist.gov/tables/Na-001.html) includes phase transitions and is not substituted for the WebBook GAS fit. Its standard pressure is not silently transferred to the GAS polynomial. Isotope composition, coefficient uncertainty and covariance remain UNKNOWN or unspecified.

Live canonical accessions and the thermal evaluation index contain no Sodium entry; no duplicate scientific record was created. All 90 Sodium files and five captured production/catalogue/proof files retain their hashes. Four focused software checks pass. Candidate transcriptions remain private and unaccessioned; exact rights, independent scientific review, source-ID allocation and fresh asset-slot review remain open. Evidence: `.mat-local/sodium-source-review-2026-10-10/numerical-review.json`, `deduplication.json`, `before.json`, and `checks.test.mjs`.

Inspect .mat-local/sodium-source-review-2026-10-10/progress.json and actual named terminal receipts before another writer starts. Finish the source-review checkpoint projection if pending. Then resolve the exact WebBook/SRD69 rights scope and independent scientific source review for the retained Sodium GAS fit and 50 publisher calculation rows. Recheck physical/manifest union table 011 and graph 013, source-ID uniqueness, dated bytes and the strict neutral root binding before accession. The 1171 printed boundary requires explicit 1170.525 K calculation metadata. No numerical Sodium accession, experimental replication or panel completion is claimed. Do not invoke the unsafe legacy intake-review producer before its preservation repair.
